The Difference

Verified Records, Not Scraped Lists

A list broker sells you names. Nocturnal Leads sells you a checked territory — every record graded, dated, and sourced before it can enter a batch.

Every Record Graded Before It Counts

Records enter the store as Candidates and earn their way up. A record only counts toward a batch at the Verified Owner tier — the venue is confirmed open, and the owner or decision-maker behind it is identified.

  • Verified Owner — venue confirmed open, owner identified
  • Verified Contact — venue confirmed, working contact on file
  • Candidate — discovered, still being checked, never sold as verified

Every record passes five checks before it can count toward a batch:

  • Licence active and trading
  • Contact published or filed
  • Email double-verified
  • Decision-maker named where findable
  • Human sign-off — re-verified at least every 90 days

No Ghosts, No Duplicates, No Dead Inboxes

The standard list fails in three ways: the venue closed, the venue appears twice, or the email bounces. Each one costs you a rep’s hour and a prospect’s patience.

Every Nocturnal Leads record carries its last-verified date and the source that proved it, so you can see the freshness of what you bought — and a record that fails re-verification never ships.

One Buyer Per Metro — Yours Alone For 30 Days

List brokers sell the same names to everyone, so five competitors call the same owner in the same week. Nocturnal Leads sells each metro batch to exactly one buyer, and that buyer holds it exclusively for 30 days.

While your exclusivity runs, the metro is closed to every other buyer. Your outreach lands in a quiet inbox, not a bidding war.

Straight To The Decision-Maker

Middlemen profit by standing between you and the venue — reselling the same contacts down a chain until the data is worthless. Nocturnal Leads cuts the chain: records are built from the venue’s own public proof and graded against the owner, not copied from another broker’s spreadsheet.

And if a record turns out to be wrong, the replace-or-credit guarantee makes it right — a bad record is replaced or credited, never argued about.

FAQ

Questions, Answered Straight

The objections every experienced buyer raises — answered the same way we run the store.

What Exactly Is A Batch?+

A batch is the set of verified venue records for one metro, sold to one buyer. It is built from the store’s Verified Owner tier — venues confirmed open, with the owner or decision-maker identified — and delivered with verified emails, fit scores, last-verified dates, and sources on every record.

What Is A Batch Not?+

A batch is verified access to real venues, first or exclusively. It is not meetings, replies, or sales. We never promise those — and no bought or scraped row is ever resold as-is. Every record is original research, checked by a human, and cites its source. No talent names, emails, or phone numbers are ever in a batch — venue and business data only.

How Does Verification Work?+

Records start as Candidates when a venue is discovered. A record becomes a Verified Contact when the venue is confirmed and a working contact is on file, and a Verified Owner when the owner or decision-maker behind the venue is identified. Today the store holds 70 records: 17 Verified Owner, 4 Verified Contact, and 49 Candidate, with 21 verified emails. Only Verified Owner records count toward a batch.

What Does One Buyer Per Metro Mean?+

Each metro batch is sold to exactly one buyer. While you hold it, no other buyer can purchase that metro’s records — so the owners in your batch are not being pitched the same week by three competitors working the same list.

How Long Does Exclusivity Last?+

30 days from delivery. During that window the metro stays closed to other buyers. When the window ends, the metro can be offered again — starting with the waitlist.

What Happens If A Record Is Bad?+

It is covered by the replace-or-credit guarantee. If a record proves wrong — the venue is closed, the contact is not who the record says, the email is dead — the record is replaced or credited within the guarantee terms. We do not guarantee your sales outcomes; we guarantee the records are what we said they are.

When Do Batches Ship?+

A metro ships its first batch when it reaches 50 Verified Owner records — the gate that keeps batches worth buying. Jacksonville, the first metro in build-out, stands at 4 of 50. No batches have been sold yet, and no buyer has been signed: the waitlist is forming now so first buyers are in position when their metro clears the gate.

Why Pay Before Access?+

Because the records are the product. Open browsing would put verified owner contacts in every competitor’s hands within a week and destroy the exclusivity buyers pay for. The sample record on this page shows exactly which fields a batch contains — payment is what unlocks the values, for one buyer, in one metro.

How Is Pricing Set?+

By territory — one metro, one state, or national — and quoted in a private sales conversation. Pricing never appears in public copy, because an exclusive territory is negotiated, not listed. Join the waitlist and your quote starts with the metro you want.
